newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Long Swedish debt yields slide in calm trade.
newsitem.headline: Long Swedish debt yields slide in calm trade.

text.p: Swedish long debt yields inched down a touch on Thursday in extremely quiet trade and the crown was stable.
A quarterly inflation report by Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, contained no surprises. The focus has now turned to the U.S. unemployment statistics on Friday.

Six-month T-bill rates were flat at 4.23 percent and the ten-year bond yields slid two basis points to 6.95 percent. The crown was stable at 4.4820 against the mark compared to 4.4830 late on Wednesday.
The Riksbank forecast Swedish consumer prices would rise two percent in 1997 and three percent in 1998.
The underlying inflation was seen at between 1.5 and 2 percent in 1997 and 1998, the Riksbank said.
The Riksbank concluded that monetary policy was well balanced and the crown was undervalued.
"The only thing our economists have read into the report is that the Riksbank seems not to be worried that a weaker crown could spark inflationary tendencies," one chief dealer said.
